egress.free_allowance: The shop page states 20 to 50 G of traffic for the free plan while the same page and the home page advertise 'unlimited traffic, no speed limit'. The two statements are on the same vendor.

chaining: Unusable for 1 TiB; at 50 GB it is a debugging tunnel.
binding_note: Even the top of the range, 50 GB, is about 0.045 TiB, so the byte quota fails first and by a wide margin.

identity_cost.detail: Registration on the console; the site says nothing about real-name on the pages read.

reliability_note: No reliability report found; the site claims 8 BGP nodes and 99.9 percent availability without evidence.
confidence_note: Both contradictory sentences are on the vendor's own shop page read. A support answer would settle which one is operative.

evidence.proved: free plan lists 20 to 50 G of traffic next to an 'unlimited traffic' headline
home page repeats 'unlimited traffic, no speed limit'

notes: This is the cleanest example in the sweep of an unlimited-traffic headline that its own pricing table contradicts. Treat the 20 to 50 GB as the number; the headline is marketing copy on the same page.

extras.wg_detail: The site advertises UDP protocol penetration and an FRP UDP option for game servers; a WG datagram fits inside, but no node list with a UDP flag was found.
